explanation: Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m².
Metformin should not be initiated when eGFR is below 45 mL/min/1.73 m².
For people already treated with metformin, reassess benefits/risks and consider dose reduction when eGFR is below 45.
SGLT2 inhibitor therapy is recommended for T2D with CKD when eGFR is at least 20.
A GLP-1 receptor agonist is preferred for glycemic management in advanced CKD with eGFR below 30.
People with type 2 diabetes should have UACR and eGFR assessed at least annually.
People with CKD should have urinary albumin and eGFR monitored 1–4 times per year depending on stage.
When eGFR is below 60, screening for CKD complications is indicated.
UACR of at least 300 mg/g is severely elevated albuminuria.
UACR 30–299 mg/g is moderately elevated albuminuria.
Individuals with eGFR below 60 receiving ACE inhibitors should have potassium and kidney function monitored periodically.
Individuals with eGFR below 60 receiving ARBs should have potassium and kidney function monitored periodically.
Individuals with eGFR below 60 receiving an MRA should have potassium and kidney function monitored periodically.
Diuretic-treated patients should be monitored for hypokalemia.
Elevated potassium in a patient receiving an ACE inhibitor requires safety review and monitoring.
Elevated potassium in a patient receiving an ARB requires safety review and monitoring.
Elevated potassium in a patient receiving an MRA requires safety review and monitoring.
Adults with hypertension and CKD should generally be treated to a BP goal below 130/80 mm Hg.
Adults with hypertension and CKD should generally be treated to a BP goal below 130/80 mm Hg.
Stage 1 hypertension includes SBP 130–139 mm Hg when DBP is below 90.
Stage 1 hypertension includes DBP 80–89 mm Hg when SBP is below 140.
Stage 2 hypertension includes SBP at least 140 mm Hg.
Stage 2 hypertension includes DBP at least 90 mm Hg.
Elevated BP is SBP 120–129 with DBP below 80.
Normal BP is below 120/80 mm Hg.
Adults 40–75 with diabetes and LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL are recommended moderate-intensity statin therapy without calculating 10-year risk.
LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL warrants high-intensity statin therapy without calculating 10-year ASCVD risk.
Clinical ASCVD should be treated with high-intensity or maximally tolerated statin therapy; LDL-C 70 is a threshold used for nonstatin consideration in very high risk.
Repeat lipid measurement 4–12 weeks after statin initiation or dose adjustment.
Adults 40–75 being evaluated for primary prevention should have ASCVD risk estimation and clinician–patient discussion before pharmacologic prevention.
Persistently elevated LDL-C ≥160 mg/dL is a risk-enhancing factor.
Persistently elevated triglycerides ≥175 mg/dL are a risk-enhancing factor.
CAC score zero can support withholding statin therapy in selected adults when higher-risk conditions are absent.
CAC 1–99 favors statin initiation in adults age 55 or older.
CAC ≥100 is a threshold supporting statin initiation in selected adults.
SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for symptomatic chronic HFrEF regardless of diabetes status.
Guideline-directed therapy for HFrEF includes RAS inhibition; ARNI is recommended as first-line when feasible.
Beta blockers are one of the guideline-directed medication classes for HFrEF.
SGLT2 inhibitors can be beneficial in HFmrEF.
SGLT2 inhibitors may be beneficial in HFpEF.
GDMT should be continued in HFimpEF to prevent relapse.
Statins remain first-line lipid-lowering therapy in chronic coronary disease.
Long-term beta-blocker therapy is not recommended solely to improve outcomes in CCD absent recent MI, LVEF ≤50%, or another indication.
Either a calcium-channel blocker or beta-blocker is recommended as first-line antianginal therapy.
Aspirin should be used infrequently for routine primary prevention because of limited net benefit.
SGLT2 inhibitor users with reduced kidney function may have increased risk of volume depletion/hypotension.
SGLT2 inhibitor users receiving loop diuretics may have increased risk of volume depletion/hypotension.
Acute illness can predispose SGLT2 inhibitor users to ketoacidosis; risk should be reviewed.
In lower eGFR ranges, exposure to nephrotoxins such as NSAIDs should be minimized.
Nephrology referral should be considered in advanced CKD with eGFR below 30.
